requirement:
The requirements index links to its documented-coverage-gaps subchapter
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index`.
rationale:
The subject has one obligation. The requirements index must link to its generated documented-coverage-gaps subchapter. Under `requirements.test-coverage.index`, this applies whether the index is explicitly placed or automatically generated. Three marked tests cover it, and each asserts the link text and target on the index content.

- **Explicitly placed index:** `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` builds a book with an index chapter at `appendix/requirements-index.md`. It asserts that the index content contains `[Documented coverage gaps](requirements-index/coverage.html)`. It also asserts that exactly one "Documented coverage gaps" child exists, with path `appendix/requirements-index/coverage.md` and parent names `["Requirements index"]`. So the link points to a real subchapter, and the relative target is correct for a nested index path.
- **Automatically generated index:** `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` has no index marker, so a default index is created. It asserts the same link, `requirements-index/coverage.html`. It also asserts that the single coverage child has path `requirements-index/coverage.md` and parent `Requirements index`.
- **Index inside a hierarchy:** `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]` runs over numbered and unnumbered parents. It asserts that the parent's content contains `[Documented coverage gaps](reports/coverage.html)`. It also asserts that the coverage chapter sits under the parent with the right path, parent names and numbering.

The tests do not restrict the link to a single form, and the subject text names no other boundary cases. The explicit-placement and automatic-generation modes are each tested, and the hierarchy test adds a third path style. No gaps found, and there are no acknowledgments.
